Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed. The card's family-config decision and GymnasiumDriver helper are used. The card's mock_strategy.preferred is upstream-sim, but the upstream simulator is a separately downloaded Windows Unreal/AirSim executable outside the clone (README.md:8 and :165-171), so there is no in-clone simulator to serve; the fake backend is a pure Python kinematic stand-in (fake.py) and was never compared with the upstream scene. The sim backend (gym.make of the legacy gym==0.21.0 registration) was not run. The fake returns the full configured 50 x 50 x 1 depth array, not a reduced stand-in, so no array is NOT COVERED. The driver sets autoreset=True so a step after a terminal state starts a new episode through the bridge; AirSimDroneEnv itself expects the caller to call reset(), and this is disclosed in fidelity.gaps along with the fake-only reset options. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge seeds the next reset without a native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the integer/array inputs the Gymnasium bridge derives (ticks, seed twice, action.values); the package does not declare actions to add units because the bridge derives those schemas. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. Only catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests.
